key_insight: Real-world immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes varied across cancers, with some patients surviving well beyond treatment discontinuation and poorer performance status associated with shorter survival.
clinical_relevance: Treatment duration alone may not capture long-term outcomes, and patient performance status is important when interpreting pivotal trial results in routine care.
method: Retrospective cohort of 3,231 adults receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors across four Belgian hospitals.
Structured and unstructured electronic health records harmonized using OMOP-CDM and natural language processing.
Survival and treatment trajectories assessed, with descriptive trial comparisons and multivariable Cox regression.
evidence_signal: Among 568 metastatic patients who discontinued immunotherapy without subsequent systemic therapy, median post-discontinuation survival was 21.4 months; ECOG ≥2 was associated with poorer overall survival than ECOG 0–1 (adjusted HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.82–2.60).
watch_item: Observational, descriptive comparisons cannot establish causal differences from trials or show that discontinuing treatment improves survival.
paper_title: Comprehensive real-world utilization, treatment trajectories, and outcomes of immune checkpoint inhibitors across cancer types: the multicenter FAIR-ICI cohort
